newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB wheat yield outlook holds on SE Prairie rains.
newsitem.headline: CWB wheat yield outlook holds on SE Prairie rains.

text.p: Western Canadian wheat yield prospects held firm on Tuesday due to scattered rainfall over the arid southeast Prairies since Saturday, a Canadian Wheat Board weather analyst said.

"The weekend rain was scattered and it cooled off, so that was a bit of a reprieve. It looks like we got five to 20 mm (0.2 to 0.8 inch) in the last two to three days. It's given us some breathing room to the end of June," said Paul Bullock, a CWB weather and crop surveillance director.
The CWB on June 11 cut its wheat yield outlook by 0.5 bushel an acre, to 29.5 to 31.5 bu/ac, on dry weather on the southeastern Prairies.
Typical yields on Prairie wheat range from 30 to 32 bu/ac.
Farmland in southeast Saskatchewan and southwest Manitoba usually produces more wheat than the Prairie average at 32 to 35 bu/ac, because of richer soil and less frequent droughts, the CWB said.
"If we get any significant precipitation later this week like they're forecasting, we won't be too concerned until the heading stage in early July," Bullock said.
The area from Winnipeg to Regina saw less than half of normal rain since April 8, Environment Canada said.

"The Canada-U.S. border south of Brandon (Manitoba) saw less than 25 percent of normal precipitation all the way to west of Estevan and east of Regina," said Brian Fehr, superintendent of the Environment Canada Winnipeg Climate Centre.
